qa_pairs.question: What types of projects are eligible to apply through the Research Platforms and Portals (RPP) process?
qa_pairs.answer: Projects applying through the RPP process must provide resources to a larger research community via a set of cloud-based tools, applications, and/or data, thus enabling them to access national resources via a common interface. They must also be able to develop, operate, and manage the proposed portal or platform with minimal support from Alliance Federation staff. Generally, these projects involve cloud resources, often through a front-end gateway on persistent virtual machines, with possible backend compute via cloud nodes or job-based submission to large national clusters, and may include large databases.

qa_pairs.question: If a research group receives a multi-year allocation through the Research Platforms and Portals (RPP) process, do they need to submit a full application every year to renew it?
qa_pairs.answer: No, research groups that are awarded multi-year allocations are required to submit an annual progress report; however, they do not need to submit a new application each year to renew. This annual progress report must be uploaded directly on CCDB.

qa_pairs.question: Can an Academic Principal Investigator (PI) submit more than one application through the Research Platforms and Portals (RPP) process?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, an Academic PI may be the lead submitter for one RPP application per competition round and can also be involved in other RPP applications as a participant. However, they can only be the lead submitter for one Resources for Research Groups (RRG) application at a time.
